title: An RDW–MCV interaction did not establish improved elevated-CRP prediction across two NHANES cycles
abstract: In 4,383 NHANES 2005–2006 adults, we fitted a conventional blood-index and demographic model for contemporaneous CRP >3 mg/L, with or without a centered RDW-by-MCV interaction. Frozen models were tested in 5,043 adults from the separately recruited 2015–2016 cycle. The added interaction changed survey-weighted Brier loss by +0.000339 (conditional Rao–Wu bootstrap 95% interval −0.000397 to +0.001114), failing the registered improvement criterion. AUC rose from 0.78432 to 0.78488, but probability calibration did not improve. The result is a scoped negative transport test, not evidence of equivalence or validation in a different study program.
